subproblems.title: H¹ along a unit-speed line is Lebesgue measure (change of variables)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, a, τ ∈ ℝ^P with |τ| = 1, and φ(u) := a + uτ for u ∈ ℝ. For every Borel set A ⊆ ℝ: (i) φ(A) is a Borel subset of ℝ^P; (ii) H¹(φ(A)) = L¹(A); (iii) ∫_{φ(A)} h dH¹ = ∫_A h(a + uτ) du for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ. Here H¹ is Mathlib's normalized Euclidean Hausdorff measure μHE[1] on ℝ^P (= EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)), L¹ is volume on ℝ, and the integrals are Bochner integrals (value 0 when not integrable).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a τ : Euclid P), ‖τ‖ = 1 → ∀ A : Set ℝ, MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet ((fun u : ℝ => a + u • τ) '' A) ∧ μHE[1] ((fun u : ℝ => a + u • τ) '' A) = volume A ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ x in (fun u : ℝ => a + u • τ) '' A, h x ∂μHE[1] = ∫ u in A, h (a + u • τ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3 (H¹ on the open segment I), generalized from (0, ℓ) to an arbitrary Borel parameter set A. Background: Simon Ch. 6, 2.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 196–208) integrates over an oriented curve against H¹, and 2.4 (lines 222–227) notes M([[M]]) = Hⁿ(M); H¹ is Mathlib's μHE[1].
Notation: φ(u) := a + uτ.
1. φ is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P. For u, v ∈ ℝ, φ(u) − φ(v) = uτ − vτ = (u − v)τ, so |φ(u) − φ(v)| = |u − v|·|τ| = |u − v| because |τ| = 1 (dist_eq_norm, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub, sub_smul, norm_smul; Isometry.of_dist_eq).
2. An isometry is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), and a closed embedding between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). So φ is injective and measurable and maps measurable sets to measurable sets. Since A is Borel, φ(A) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). This is conclusion (i).
3. On ℝ, μHE[1] is Lebesgue measure. InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume with V = ℝ gives μHE[finrank ℝ ℝ] = volume, and finrank ℝ ℝ = 1.
4. Measure of φ(A). μHE[1] is invariant under isometries for arbitrary sets (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), so μHE[1](φ(A)) = μHE[1](A), the right side taken on ℝ. By step 3 this equals volume(A). This is conclusion (ii).
5. Restricted measure. Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives φ_#(μHE[1] on ℝ) = μHE[1]⌞range φ. Restrict both sides to φ(A).
   - Left side: for a measurable embedding, (φ_#μ)⌞S = φ_#(μ⌞φ⁻¹(S)) for every S (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). With S = φ(A) and φ⁻¹(φ(A)) = A (injectivity, Injective.preimage_image), it becomes φ_#(μHE[1]⌞A).
   - Right side: (μHE[1]⌞range φ)⌞φ(A) = μHE[1]⌞(φ(A) ∩ range φ) by Measure.restrict_restrict (φ(A) is measurable by step 2), and this is μHE[1]⌞φ(A) because φ(A) ⊆ range φ.
   Combining with step 3: μHE[1]⌞φ(A) = φ_#(L¹⌞A).
6. Integral. Let h : ℝ^P → ℝ be arbitrary. By step 5, ∫_{φ(A)} h dH¹ = ∫ h d(φ_#(L¹⌞A)). By MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map this equals ∫_A h(φ(u)) du = ∫_A h(a + uτ) du. That lemma holds for every function h, with no measurability or integrability hypothesis, because φ is a measurable embedding. This is conclusion (iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: φ(u) = a + uτ is an isometry ℝ → ℝ^P because |τ| = 1, hence a closed and measurable embedding, so φ(A) is Borel.
μHE[1] on ℝ is Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, finrank ℝ ℝ = 1).
φ_#H¹ = H¹⌞range φ; restricting to φ(A) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, Measure.restrict_restrict, injectivity) gives H¹⌞φ(A) = φ_#(L¹⌞A).
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map turns ∫_{φ(A)} h dH¹ into ∫_A h(a + uτ) du for every h.

subproblems.title: Every point of an open segment has approximate tangent line span{τ}
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, a, τ ∈ ℝ^P with |τ| = 1, ℓ ∈ ℝ, and I := {a + uτ : 0 < u < ℓ} (the image of the open interval (0, ℓ) under u ↦ a + uτ). For every x ∈ I, the subspace Q := span{τ} is the 1-dimensional approximate tangent space of I at x in Simon's sense (Ch. 3, 1.4), i.e. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q: finrank Q = 1, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(I)} f dH¹ → ∫_Q f dH¹ as r → 0⁺. Here η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is blowUpMap x r and H¹ = μHE[1].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a τ : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), ‖τ‖ = 1 → ∀ x ∈ (fun u : ℝ => a + u • τ) '' Ioo 0 ℓ, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 ((fun u : ℝ => a + u • τ) '' Ioo 0 ℓ) x (Submodule.span ℝ {τ})
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5; Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–85). That definition says the n-dimensional subspace P is the approximate tangent space of M at x if ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C⁰_c, where η_{x,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x); in Lean this map is blowUpMap x λ.
Notation: φ(u) := a + uτ, I := φ((0, ℓ)), Q := span{τ}, η_r := blowUpMap x r, H¹ := μHE[1].
1. Let x ∈ I and write x = φ(s₀) with 0 < s₀ < ℓ. Since |τ| = 1, τ ≠ 0, so finrank Q = 1 (finrank_span_singleton). This is the dimension condition.
2. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its topological support is compact (f.hasCompactSupport), hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) for some R₀. Put ρ := max(R₀, 1) > 0. If f(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ tsupport f (subset_tsupport), so |y| ≤ R₀ ≤ ρ.
3. Put δ := min(s₀, ℓ − s₀). Then δ > 0, δ ≤ s₀ and δ ≤ ℓ − s₀. Fix r with 0 < r < δ/ρ; then rρ < δ.
4. η_r(I) ⊆ Q. For u ∈ (0, ℓ), η_r(φ(u)) = r⁻¹((a + uτ) − (a + s₀τ)) = (r⁻¹(u − s₀))τ. This is a scalar multiple of τ, hence lies in Q (Submodule.mem_span_singleton).
5. f vanishes on Q ∖ η_r(I). Let y ∈ Q with f(y) ≠ 0. By Submodule.mem_span_singleton, y = cτ for some c ∈ ℝ, and |c| = |cτ| = |y| ≤ ρ by step 2. Put u := s₀ + rc. Then |rc| = r|c| ≤ rρ < δ, so u ≥ s₀ − |rc| > s₀ − δ ≥ 0 and u ≤ s₀ + |rc| < s₀ + δ ≤ ℓ. Hence u ∈ (0, ℓ), and by step 4, η_r(φ(u)) = (r⁻¹(rc))τ = cτ = y, so y ∈ η_r(I). Contrapositively, f(y) = 0 for every y ∈ Q ∖ η_r(I).
6. Q is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence Borel and in particular null-measurable. Apply setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero with t := Q and s := η_r(I): s ⊆ t by step 4, and f = 0 everywhere (so a.e.) on t ∖ s by step 5. The lemma does not need s to be measurable. It gives ∫_Q f dH¹ = ∫_{η_r(I)} f dH¹ for every r ∈ (0, δ/ρ).
7. Since δ/ρ > 0, the interval (0, δ/ρ) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). By step 6, r ↦ ∫_{η_r(I)} f dH¹ is eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0 to the constant ∫_Q f dH¹, so it tends to ∫_Q f dH¹ (tendsto_const_nhds.congr'). As f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) was arbitrary, this together with step 1 is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Write x = a + s₀τ with 0 < s₀ < ℓ; finrank span{τ} = 1 because τ ≠ 0.
For f ∈ C_c, f(y) ≠ 0 implies |y| ≤ ρ for some ρ > 0; put δ := min(s₀, ℓ − s₀) > 0.
For 0 < r < δ/ρ: blowUpMap x r '' I ⊆ span{τ}, and every y = cτ with f(y) ≠ 0 equals blowUpMap x r (a + (s₀ + rc)τ) with s₀ + rc ∈ (0, ℓ).
So for all small r the integral over the blow-up equals the integral over the closed line span{τ} (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).
Eventually constant in 𝓝[>] 0, hence convergent: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x span{τ}.

subproblems.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus for a smooth 0-form along a segment
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let g be a C^∞ differential 0-form on ℝ^P (IsSmoothForm g). For every a, v ∈ ℝ^P and ℓ ≥ 0: ∫_{(0,ℓ)} (dg)(a + uv)(v) du = g(a + ℓv)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩. Here dg = exteriorDerivative g is a 1-form, (dg)(y)(v) is the value of the 1-covector dg(y) on the 1-tuple (v), and g(y)⟨⟩ is the value of the 0-covector g(y) on the empty tuple (fun i => i.elim0). The integral is the Lebesgue (Bochner) integral over the open interval (0, ℓ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 0), IsSmoothForm g → ∀ (a v : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), 0 ≤ ℓ → ∫ u in Ioo 0 ℓ, exteriorDerivative g (a + u • v) (fun _ => v) = g (a + ℓ • v) (fun i => i.elim0) - g a (fun i => i.elim0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 8; Simon Ch. 6, 2.3 (chapter-06.txt lines 214–218: ∂T(ω) = T(dω)), which is motivated by Stokes' theorem (lines 210–213). In dimension one Stokes' theorem is the fundamental theorem of calculus.
Notation: ⟨⟩ := (fun i => i.elim0), the unique tuple Fin 0 → ℝ^P; ĝ(y) := g(y)⟨⟩ ∈ ℝ.
1. Smoothness of ĝ. ĝ = ev ∘ g, where ev := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ ℝ^P ℝ ⟨⟩ (α ↦ α⟨⟩) is a continuous linear map. A continuous linear map composed with the C^∞ map g is C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp). In particular ĝ is C¹ and differentiable everywhere, and y ↦ Dĝ(y) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv). Also g itself is differentiable (ContDiff.differentiable, since the smoothness order ∞ ≠ 0).
2. Value of dg on a 1-tuple. Since g is differentiable at y, exteriorDerivative_apply (= extDeriv_apply) gives, for w : Fin 1 → ℝ^P,
   dg(y)(w) = Σ_{i : Fin 1} (−1)^i · D(z ↦ g(z)(Fin.removeNth i w))(y)(w i) = D(z ↦ g(z)(Fin.removeNth 0 w))(y)(w 0),
   using Fin.sum_univ_succ and (−1)^0 = 1. For w = (fun _ => v), Fin.removeNth 0 w is a map Fin 0 → ℝ^P, so it equals ⟨⟩ (the type Fin 0 → ℝ^P is a subsingleton). Hence dg(y)(v) = Dĝ(y)v for every y ∈ ℝ^P.
3. Chain rule. For each u ∈ ℝ, the map u ↦ a + uv has derivative v at u (hasDerivAt_id, HasDerivAt.smul_const, HasDerivAt.const_add). ĝ has Fréchet derivative Dĝ(a + uv) at a + uv (step 1). So u ↦ ĝ(a + uv) has derivative Dĝ(a + uv)v at u (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt).
4. Integrability. u ↦ Dĝ(a + uv)v is continuous: it is the continuous map Dĝ (step 1), composed with the continuous u ↦ a + uv and evaluated at the fixed vector v. Hence it is interval integrable on [0, ℓ] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable).
5. Conclusion. Since ℓ ≥ 0 and singletons are Lebesgue-null, ∫_{(0,ℓ)} F du = ∫_{(0,ℓ]} F du = ∫_0^ℓ F du for every F (integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). Rewrite the integrand pointwise by step 2, then apply the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt with steps 3–4):
   ∫_{(0,ℓ)} dg(a + uv)(v) du = ∫_0^ℓ Dĝ(a + uv)v du = ĝ(a + ℓv) − ĝ(a + 0·v) = g(a + ℓv)⟨⟩ − g(a)⟨⟩. ∎
proof_key_steps: ĝ := g(·)⟨⟩ = ev_⟨⟩ ∘ g is C^∞, with continuous derivative.
extDeriv_apply on a 1-tuple: dg(y)(v) = Dĝ(y)v, because removeNth 0 of a 1-tuple is the empty tuple.
Chain rule: d/du ĝ(a + uv) = Dĝ(a + uv)v, which is continuous in u.
For ℓ ≥ 0, ∫ over (0,ℓ) equals the interval integral ∫_0^ℓ, and the FTC gives ĝ(a + ℓv) − ĝ(a).

subproblems.title: The oriented open segment with multiplicity one is an IMRep
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, a, τ ∈ ℝ^P with |τ| = 1, and ℓ > 0. There is an integer multiplicity triple R (structure IMRep of the frozen contract, Simon 6.3.1) of degree 1 in U = ℝ^P such that: (i) R.carrier ⊆ [a, a + ℓτ] (segment ℝ a (a + ℓ • τ)); (ii) R.measure(ℝ^P) < ∞; (iii) R.action(ω) = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(a + uτ)(τ) du for every differential 1-form ω on ℝ^P, where ω(y)(τ) is the value of the 1-covector ω(y) on the 1-tuple (τ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (a τ : Euclid P) (ℓ : ℝ), ‖τ‖ = 1 → 0 < ℓ → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, R.carrier ⊆ segment ℝ a (a + ℓ • τ) ∧ R.measure univ < ∞ ∧ ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1, R.action ω = ∫ u in Ioo 0 ℓ, ω (a + u • τ) (fun _ => τ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 2–7 and 9 (the IMRep (I, 1, ζ₀) of the oriented open segment); Simon Ch. 6, 2.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 196–208) and 3.1 (lines 733–747). Definition 3.1 requires T = τ(M, θ, ξ) with M countably n-rectifiable, θ positive, integer-valued and locally Hⁿ-integrable, and ξ orienting the approximate tangent spaces Hⁿ-a.e. Uses the sibling children line_hausdorff and open_segment_tangent.
Notation: φ(u) := a + uτ, I := φ((0, ℓ)), Q := span{τ}, H¹ := μHE[1].
1. Measure facts. Apply line_hausdorff to P, a, τ (|τ| = 1) and the Borel set A := (0, ℓ). It gives: I is Borel; H¹(I) = volume((0, ℓ)) = ofReal(ℓ − 0) < ∞ (Real.volume_Ioo); and ∫_I h dH¹ = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} h(a + uτ) du for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ.
2. Orientation. Let ζ₀ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ ℝ^P ℝ (fun _ : Fin 1 => τ). This is the 1-vector with ζ₀(α) = α(τ) for every 1-covector α (by definition; apply_apply). ζ₀ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf, first alternative), witnessed by the family e := (fun _ : Fin 1 => τ):
   (i) e is orthonormal. By orthonormal_iff_ite it suffices that ⟨e i, e j⟩ is 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise. Fin 1 has only i = j = 0, and ⟨τ, τ⟩ = |τ|² = 1.
   (ii) range e = {τ} (Set.range_const), so span(range e) = Q.
   (iii) ζ₀(α) = α(e) for every α.
3. Rectifiability. Define F : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) → ℝ^P by F(w) := a + w₀τ. It is 1-Lipschitz: |F(w) − F(w')| = |(w₀ − w'₀)τ| = |(w − w')₀| ≤ |w − w'| (PiLp.norm_apply_le; LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul). For u ∈ (0, ℓ), φ(u) = F(EuclideanSpace.single 0 u), so I ⊆ range F. By countablyRectifiable_range and CountablyRectifiable.mono, I is countably 1-rectifiable.
4. Definition of R. Set carrier := I, mult := (fun _ => 1), orient := (fun _ => ζ₀). The IMRep fields hold:
   - measurableSet_carrier: by step 1.
   - carrier_subset: I ⊆ univ.
   - rectifiable: by step 3.
   - measurable_mult: a constant is measurable.
   - mult_pos: 0 < 1.
   - locallyIntegrable_mult: for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫⁻_{I∩K} 1 dH¹ = H¹(I ∩ K) (lintegral_const, Measure.restrict_apply MeasurableSet.univ, univ_inter), and H¹(I ∩ K) ≤ H¹(I) < ∞ (measure_mono, step 1).
   - aestronglyMeasurable_orient: a constant is a.e. strongly measurable.
   - orients: for every x ∈ I, open_segment_tangent (applied to P, a, τ, ℓ, |τ| = 1 and x ∈ I) gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I x Q, and step 2 gives IsUnitOrientationOf ζ₀ Q. Since I is measurable, a property of every point of I holds H¹⌞I-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem).
5. Carrier in the closed segment. Let u ∈ (0, ℓ) and t := u/ℓ. Then t ∈ [0, 1] because 0 < u ≤ ℓ and ℓ > 0 (div_nonneg, div_le_one). Moreover a + t((a + ℓτ) − a) = a + (u/ℓ)(ℓτ) = a + uτ = φ(u) (div_mul_cancel₀). By segment_eq_image' (segment x y = {x + t(y − x) : t ∈ [0, 1]}), φ(u) ∈ segment ℝ a (a + ℓτ). Hence R.carrier ⊆ segment ℝ a (a + ℓτ), which is conclusion (i).
6. Finite total measure. R.measure = (H¹⌞I).withDensity(x ↦ (1 : ℝ≥0∞)), so R.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_{ℝ^P} 1 d(H¹⌞I) (withDensity_apply on the measurable set univ, Measure.restrict_univ). By lintegral_const this is H¹(I), which is < ∞ by step 1. This is conclusion (ii).
7. Action. For every 1-form ω, R.action(ω) = ∫_I (1 : ℝ)·ζ₀(ω(x)) dH¹(x) = ∫_I ω(x)(τ) dH¹(x) (Nat.cast_one, one_mul, step 2). By step 1 with h(x) := ω(x)(τ), this equals ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(a + uτ)(τ) du, which is conclusion (iii).
Steps 4–7 give the required R. ∎
proof_key_steps: line_hausdorff with A = (0, ℓ): I is Borel, H¹(I) = ℓ < ∞, and ∫_I h dH¹ = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} h(a + uτ) du.
ζ₀ = (α ↦ α(τ)) is a unit orientation of span{τ}: the family (τ) is orthonormal and spans the line.
I lies in the range of the 1-Lipschitz map F(w) = a + w₀τ on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1), so it is countably 1-rectifiable.
R := (I, 1, ζ₀) satisfies every IMRep field; orients follows from open_segment_tangent at every point of I.
I ⊆ [a, a + ℓτ]; R.measure(ℝ^P) = H¹(I) < ∞; R.action(ω) = ∫_{(0,ℓ)} ω(a + uτ)(τ) du.
